headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP and secret-handling surface can amplify Prefect-driven workflows into leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Prefect can move workflow metadata through automation, and TREK explicitly uses browsers and MCP in a real-time collaborative tool. That creates a plausible bridge where TREK content could be treated as instructions by Prefect-driven automation. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into Prefect tasks without sanitization
IF an MCP tool call forwards browser-derived text into Prefect automation
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data separator in the handoff
Strip or escape markup before Prefect consumes TREK output
Disable MCP tool calls for untrusted TREK content
Review one sample workflow for prompt-like strings
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and files under ./data and ./uploads, while Prefect has broad network egress and API-calling capability. If Prefect ingests TREK workspace data, it can transmit sensitive material outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use and the blast radius includes secrets and personal travel records.
conditions: IF Prefect tasks read TREK files or logs
IF TREK secrets are present in shared inputs or exports
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Restrict Prefect egress to required endpoints only
Rotate any API keys exposed in TREK artifacts
Check ./data/logs/trek.log for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents onto separate storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect is an automation/orchestration system and TREK is collaborative with real-time multi-instance support and mutable files. Even without explicit write permissions listed for Prefect, the pair can still contend over shared workflow artifacts or TREK files if connected through the same workspace. Uncertainty about actual write surfaces pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF Prefect updates artifacts that TREK also edits in real time
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one writer during batch updates
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Verify whether Prefect writes into ./data or ./uploads
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable. Prefect can generate workflow metadata and automate downstream steps. If Prefect output is consumed by TREK without verification, errors can cascade into user-visible plans, reservations, or other actions. The interaction is inferred, but the blast radius is substantial.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Prefect-produced outputs as authoritative
IF downstream actions are triggered from those outputs without human review
mitigations: Insert a validation step before TREK consumes Prefect output
Require human approval for reservation-affecting actions
Compare Prefect output against source data
Log provenance for each automated handoff
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive travel and identity data, including country visit history, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If those TREK data classes flow through Prefect, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-risk inference.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is routed through Prefect logs or external APIs
IF retention settings differ between TREK storage and Prefect outputs
mitigations: Classify TREK fields before sending them onward
Disable logging of secrets and confirmation numbers
Review retention settings for both systems
Confirm residency requirements for any external API calls
requires-engineering: align data-processing agreements and retention policy
